Fans choice of Newcastle United team v Crystal Palace with the votes now counted

The votes now counted and this is the fans choice of Newcastle United team v Crystal Palace.

Actual Article Body:
The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

On Sunday morning we asked fans, which 11 players would you pick in the Newcastle United team v Crystal Palace?

Matthias Jaissle and his players looking to bounce back from consecutive defeats. Newcastle United losing to Coventry and Aston Villa.

The new Newcastle United Head Coach having now overseen four wins, two draws and three defeats in the opening two months of the season.

Today a 2pm kick-off away at Selhurst Park.

We just wanted to get a quick snapshot of what fans were thinking.

Which eleven players did you think Matthias Jaissle should select against Crystal Palace?

We put together a list of the 20 players who could potentially be selected for this game.

On Friday at his pre-match press conference, Matthias Jaissle gave a little more away than normal regarding injuries/fitness. Ewen Jaouen and Tino Livramento now the only Newcastle United players definitely ruled out of making today’s matchday squad.

Hopefully returning to today’s 20 man squad are Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey, though Matthias Jaissle making clear it will be a place on the bench at best for the pair. Nico Gonzalez and Joelinton have made it back into the starting eleven since the international break and it appears the likes of Dan Burn, Amar Dedic and William Osula could now be in a position to start, if selected.

Matthias Jaissle though revealed that Matias Fernandez-Pardo is a doubt for this game due to illness.

So here is the NUFC fans collective choice of Newcastle United team v Crystal Palace (Percentage of fans voting for each player, rounded up to the nearest whole number):

Top eleven:

100% Hall
95% Dedic
90% Gonzalez
89% Barnes
88% Burn
84% Hornicek
81% Steur
80% Osula
72% Joelinton
63% Thiaw
47% Schar

The rest:

45% Lewis Miley
43% Fernandez-Pardo
40% Wissa
38% Toure
16% Pope
10% Willock
8% Murphy
7% Botman
6% Bamba

An interesting choice of Newcastle United team v Crystal Palace from the NUFC fans who voted.

United Airlines CEO wants a wealth tax, but Americans deserve to keep their legacy

United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby's call for a near-100% inheritance tax sparks fierce debate over property rights and the American Dream.

Actual Article Body:

Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

United CEO Scott Kirby faces backlash after proposing a national wealth tax and a near-100% inheritance tax. Patrice Onwuka of the Independent Women's Forum slams Kirby's proposal.

United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby advocates for a national wealth tax and an inheritance tax approaching 100% on amounts exceeding a threshold.

My response is simple: Washington should not become the principal beneficiary of the American Dream.

According to reporting highlighted by Fox Business, Kirby believes wealth inequality requires a national response. He has every right to make that argument. But a proposal to confiscate nearly everything above a government-determined threshold deserves a forceful challenge.

LET SOCIALISTS ROB FROM THE RICH 100% AND YOU STILL WON’T BE ABLE TO PAY THE BILLS

The ability to build something and leave it to your family is one of the most powerful incentives in our economy. Treating that aspiration as a social problem would send America in precisely the wrong direction.

United CEO Scott Kirby wants both a wealth tax and a near-100% estate tax. (United Airlines)

As the founder of Engineered Tax Services, I have spent my career working with people who build businesses, invest in communities and create jobs. Their wealth often exists in operating companies, buildings, equipment and ownership interests. Those assets are productive — and frequently illiquid.

NEWSOM BEGS CALIFORNIANS TO VOTE 'NO' ON BILLIONAIRE'S TAX IN FACE OF MASS EXODUS, PITCHES NATIONWIDE TAX HIKE

A business valuation does not mean a business owner has that amount sitting in a checking account. Yet an annual wealth tax could demand cash based on an estimated asset value, even when the owner has received no corresponding income. Where does the money come from?

Depending on the rules, owners could have to borrow, sell assets or withdraw capital from their businesses. Money that might have funded equipment, expansion or hiring could instead go toward paying a tax on continued ownership. Supporters must explain why that tradeoff would serve the workers whose opportunities depend on those investments.

FORMER WASHINGTON GOVERNOR RIPS HER OWN PARTY FOR PUSHING MILLIONAIRES OUT

The inheritance proposal raises an even more fundamental question: Who should decide what happens to a lifetime of work? Parents often sacrifice because they want their children to have greater security and opportunity. Entrepreneurs take risks knowing that success could benefit their families long after they are gone. That motivation deserves respect — and drives real economic growth.

Kirby reportedly has not specified the threshold at which inheritance taxes should approach 100%. That omission matters. Nobody should pretend his remarks establish a detailed proposal affecting every family business.

THE DSA’S DANGEROUS FINE PRINT. THEY'RE COMING FOR MILLIONAIRES (AND YOU)

But even at an extremely high threshold, the principle remains troubling. A near-total marginal tax would give government an overwhelming claim on the portion of an estate above its chosen limit. Why should Washington have a stronger claim to that property than the people its owner chooses to support? Why should an arbitrary number set by the government determine the extent of one person’s property rights relative to another’s?

Advocates will argue that inherited wealth can entrench privilege. That concern deserves a serious response. Birth should never determine the limits of a person's opportunity. But neither should the government.

DAVID MARCUS: WHY ABDUL EL-SAYED’S ANTI-BILLIONAIRE SCREEDS MAY NOT PLAY IN GRAND RAPIDS

Confiscating a successful family's legacy does not, by itself, equip another family to build one. And elected officials don’t have a great track record when it comes to managing budgets and programs.

A business valuation does not mean a business owner has that amount sitting in a checking account. Yet an annual wealth tax could demand cash based on an estimated asset value, even when the owner has received no corresponding income. Where does the money come from?

We should judge policy by whether it helps more Americans become owners: start a company, purchase property, acquire useful skills, secure financing and accumulate savings.

CONSERVATIVES CAN FIGHT THE RISE OF SOCIALISM BY DEFENDING THE AMERICAN FAMILY

That is where my commitment to tax equality comes from. Too many small businesses lack access to the expertise, incentives and opportunities that sophisticated organizations know how to use. Expanding that access offers a practical path toward broader prosperity.

Also, be honest about taxation: Some accumulated wealth reflects income already taxed; some reflects appreciation that has not yet been taxed. Sound reasoning against confiscatory taxation does not require pretending every dollar has the same history. It requires recognizing that taxes change incentives — and that property rights should remain meaningful even when an owner becomes extraordinarily successful.

Kirby's reported willingness to pay these taxes himself does not settle the issue. Public policy must account for people with different assets, obligations and circumstances. One executive's willingness cannot substitute for a workable national policy.

America needs vigorous competition, fewer barriers to business formation and more pathways to financial independence. We should challenge special favors that protect incumbents and make it harder for newcomers to compete.

And we should demand that government demonstrate discipline with the resources it already receives before granting it sweeping new claims on private wealth.

The American promise is that effort, risk and perseverance can create something lasting.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

We should strengthen that promise for families still trying to get ahead.
